In the Next.js App Router repo at /opt/nxeon, the root layout at app/layout.tsx sets:

```
alternates: { canonical: "/" }
```

inside its `generateMetadata()` export (around line 80). In Next.js App Router, a route segment's `metadata`/`generateMetadata` fields are NOT deep-merged with the parent layout's for non-primitive keys like `alternates` — a child that doesn't specify `alternates.canonical` at all inherits the parent's value verbatim, while a child that does specify its own `alternates` object overrides the parent's entirely (not merged key-by-key).

I need to know: how many pages/routes in this codebase (under app/, especially app/(marketing)/**, app/blog/**, app/(marketing)/tools/**, and any programmatic/dynamic route like app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx or location-landing pages) do NOT set their own `alternates: { canonical: ... }` (or `alternates.canonical`) in their metadata/generateMetadata export? If most pages DO set their own canonical, then the root layout's "/" default is harmless (only ever applies to the homepage itself, which needs "/" anyway). If a meaningful number of pages (blog posts, tool pages, marketing landing pages, comparison pages, migrate-from pages, etc.) do NOT set a canonical, then every one of those pages would emit `<link rel="canonical" href="https://nxeon.cloud/">` pointing at the homepage instead of their own URL — a real duplicate-canonical SEO bug that could suppress indexing of secondary pages.

Please:
1. Grep across app/ (excluding node_modules, .next) for `generateMetadata`, `export const metadata`, and `alternates` to build a picture of which routes set canonical and which don't.
2. Spot-check a representative sample: app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx, a few files under app/(marketing)/tools/*/page.tsx, app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx (the catch-all, if it exists), 2-3 static marketing pages like app/(marketing)/vps/page.tsx or app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx, and any location-landing page generator (search for "locationLandings" usage in a page.tsx).
3. Report back: (a) does app/layout.tsx really set alternates.canonical to "/" unconditionally as I described — quote the exact surrounding code; (b) a list of specific example files that DO set their own canonical and ones that do NOT; (c) your best estimate of how many total routes are affected (rough count is fine, doesn't need to be exhaustive); (d) if you find that Next.js actually does something smarter here (e.g., automatically deriving canonical per-route even without explicit alternates, or the root default not applying the way I think), say so clearly since that would change the conclusion.

This is pure research — do not edit any files. Reply with a concise report (under 400 words) covering all the numbered points above, with exact file paths and line numbers for your key evidence.

content.text:
## Report

**(a) Root layout confirmed.** `/opt/nxeon/app/layout.tsx`, inside `generateMetadata()` (async function, lines 39–104), unconditionally returns:
```
alternates: { canonical: "/" },   // line 80
```
No conditional logic wraps it — every request that doesn't override `alternates` in its own metadata inherits this literal `"/"`.

**(b) Sample findings.**

Set their own canonical correctly:
- `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx:38` — `alternates: { canonical: \`/blog/${post.slug}\` }`
- `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx:55` — `alternates: { canonical: \`/${slug}\` }` (this is the programmatic location-landing catch-all, driven by `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` `COMBOS`/`LANDING_SLUGS` — confirmed correct, not part of the bug)
- `app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:27` — `alternates: { canonical: "/pricing" }`
- All 15 `app/(marketing)/tools/*/page.tsx` files (base64, dns-lookup, whois checked directly) each set their own `alternates.canonical`
- All migrate-from-*, vps-vs-*, and *-server-hosting comparison/game pages set their own canonical (confirmed via grep, ~60+ files)

Do NOT set `alternates` at all (only plain `title`/other metadata fields), so they silently inherit `"/"`:
- `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx:18`
- `app/(marketing)/affiliate/page.tsx:16`
- `app/(marketing)/block-storage/page.tsx:16`
- `app/(marketing)/business-email/page.tsx:21`
- `app/(marketing)/contact/page.tsx:10`
- `app/(marketing)/developers/page.tsx:16`
- `app/(marketing)/docs/page.tsx:6`
- `app/(marketing)/domains/page.tsx:12`
- `app/(marketing)/features/page.tsx:29`
- `app/(marketing)/security/page.tsx:18`
- `app/(marketing)/v2/page.tsx:15`
- `app/(marketing)/vibe-coding/page.tsx:14`
- `app/(marketing)/vps/page.tsx:30`
- `app/(marketing)/web-hosting/page.tsx:16`

**(c) Estimate.** Of 103 `page.tsx` files under `app/(marketing)/**` + `app/blog/**` with metadata, exactly **14 static marketing pages** lack `alternates` entirely (verified via `comm` diff of metadata-files vs. alternates-files — no false positives on spot check). All blog posts, tool pages, comparison pages, migrate-from pages, and the programmatic location-landing catch-all correctly set their own canonical, so the bug is real but scoped: 14 real routes (About, Affiliate, Block Storage, Business Email, Contact, Developers, Docs, Domains, Features, Security, v2, Vibe Coding, **VPS** — a core product page — and Web Hosting) all emit `<link rel="canonical" href="https://nxeon.cloud/">`, telling Google to consolidate them into the homepage instead of indexing them individually.

**(d) No smarter Next.js behavior.** Next.js App Router does not auto-derive canonical URLs per-route from the pathname; `alternates` is metadata you must set explicitly, and it is shallow-merged with the parent (non-primitive keys like `alternates` are replaced wholesale, not deep-merged), exactly as you described. The 14 files above have no `alternates` key in their metadata object at all, so nothing overrides the parent's `"/"` — this is a genuine duplicate-canonical bug affecting those 14 pages, `/vps` being the most consequential.
